539	---
540	title: "Sound at high speed"
541	description: "Why a clip goes silent above ×12, what the alert asks before it happens, and how ramps count towards the limit."
542	---
543	
544	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
545	
546	A clip that plays faster than ×12 loses its sound in the preview and in the export, while its picture keeps playing. Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip there.
547	
548	<AtAGlance
549	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…']}
550	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The ⌥ rate stretch on the timeline']}
551	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action_end', 'retime_range']}
552	/>
553	
554	## Sound is left out above ×12
555	
556	The limit is the same with [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) on or off. At exactly ×12 the sound still plays, and at anything faster it doesn't. The picture carries on to the top of the speed range, ×1000.
557	
558	The limit is fixed, and no setting changes it. It sits a margin below the speeds at which an export with sound can stall.
559	
560	Nothing is deleted. Bring the clip back to ×12 or below and its sound returns.
561	
562	## The alert
563	
564	Before an edit takes a clip with sound from ×12 or below to above ×12, an alert asks first. For one clip it reads:
565	
566	> “Interview” will be silent at ×16.
567	>
568	> Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The picture still plays.
569	
570	For several clips it counts them. It reads “3 clips will be silent at ×16.”, or “3 clips will be silent at their new speeds.” when their rates differ, and then “Frame Job leaves a clip’s audio out above ×12. The pictures still play.”
571	
572	The alert is a question, not a block. You can always go ahead.
573	
574	| Button | What it does |
575	| --- | --- |
576	| **Set Speed** | Makes the edit exactly as you asked. It's the default button, and it keeps this name when the edit is a ramp or a stretch. |
577	| **Cancel** | Changes nothing and adds no undo step. |
578	
579	You're asked once. A clip that's already above ×12 isn't asked about again, even if you make it faster still. A clip whose sound is switched off, or whose file has no sound, isn't asked about at all.
580	
581	## Where the alert appears
582	
583	| You're using | If you choose **Cancel** |
584	| --- | --- |
585	| **Clip ▸ Speed…** | The sheet stays open. |
586	| **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The sheet stays open. |
587	| **Clip ▸ Retime Range…** | The sheet stays open. |
588	| **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The sheet stays open. |
589	| The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/): **Rate**, its quick picks, **Keep pitch**, **Reset** or **Fit to** | The fields go back to what they showed. |
590	| The [⌥ rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) | The clip stays as it was before the drag. |
591	
592	A stretch is put back when you let go, so nothing has changed while the question is up. **Set Speed** then applies it again.
593	
594	Moving, resizing or removing an action can't raise a clip's fastest rate, so those edits never ask.
595	
596	## Ramps and the ×12 rule
597	
598	On a [ramped clip](/speed/speed-ramps/), Frame Job looks at the fastest rate set anywhere on the clip. If any rate in the ramp is above ×12, the whole clip is silent, not only the fast part.
599	
600	The alert counts the ramp's peak rate in the same way. A clip at ×1 with one Speed action ending at ×16 is asked about at ×16.
601	
602	An end rate on an action lying past the clip's end still counts, even though that part never plays. If a trimmed clip has gone silent for no clear reason, check the count in the header of its [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) in the Clip tab. An action wholly past the clip's end has no band you can reach, but it's still counted.
603	
604	## The silent audio note
605	
606	The Speed section shows **Audio is silent above ×12** while a selected clip is past the limit. It needs a clip whose file has sound and whose sound is on. It appears in either pitch mode, and a ramp counts by its fastest rate.
607	
608	## Good to know
609	
610	- A clip that only has sound follows the same rule, and is silent above ×12.
611	- Clips inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) count too.
612	- Turning a clip's sound back on while it's above ×12 doesn't bring up the alert, because the speed didn't change. The silent audio note shows instead.
613	- When Speed Up Typing runs by itself after a [recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/), Frame Job can't stop to ask. A speed-up that would silence a clip isn't made, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector.
614	
615	## With an agent
616	
617	An agent is never asked. Its edit goes through, and the result lists the ids of the clips that went silent in `audio_left_out`, with a sentence saying so in `audio_note`. Neither appears if no clip crossed the limit. See [Above ×12 the sound is left out](/mcp/tools-speed/#above-12-the-sound-is-left-out).
618

627	title: "Speed ramps"
628	description: "What a speed ramp is, how Speed actions build one, how to read it on the timeline, and why a ramp can't play past the end of its file."
629	---
630	
631	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
632	
633	A speed ramp changes a clip's rate over time. It can play at ×1, speed up to ×4 over half a second, hold there, and slow back down, all inside one clip. Use one to hurry through a slow stretch or linger on a moment, without cutting the clip or moving anything after it.
634	
635	<AtAGlance
636	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Add Action']}
637	  keys="⌥⌘K"
638	  where={['The action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section']}
639	  tools={['add_speed_ramp', 'add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action', 'remove_action']}
640	/>
641	
642	There are two ways to make one:
643	
644	- [Make a speed ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**, which builds a whole ramp in one step.
645	- [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/), one change of speed at a time.
646	
647	Both give you the same thing, so you can start from the sheet and adjust the result by hand.
648	
649	## Speed actions
650	
651	A ramp is made of Speed actions. A Speed action is an ordinary [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip's action lane whose end sets a rate. Each one:
652	
653	- starts from the rate the clip is playing at when the action begins, which is the clip's own rate or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on
654	- moves to its own end rate along its curve
655	- keeps that end rate after it finishes, until the next Speed action
656	
657	So a ramp up and back down is two actions. The first ends at ×4, the clip stays at ×4 after it, and the second ends at ×1.
658	
659	An end rate can be anything from ×0.1 to ×1000. Only a video or audio clip can have one, because only those have a file to read at a rate.
660	
661	## A ramped clip keeps its place
662	
663	A ramp changes how much of the file plays, not where the clip sits. The clip's start, its end and every clip around it stay put.
664	
665	Speeding part of a clip up makes it play further into its file. Slowing part of it down makes it play less of the file.
666	
667	For example, take a 10-second clip at ×1 with a Linear ramp up to ×4 from 2 s to 2.5 s, and back to ×1 from 4 s to 4.5 s. It still takes 10 seconds on the timeline, but it now plays 16 seconds of its file.
668	
669	This is the difference from [Change a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), where the clip gets longer or shorter.
670	
671	## Never past the end of the file
672	
673	Because a ramp can play further into the file, it can run out of file. A ramp may never play past the end of the clip's media, so an edit that would do that isn't made, and the reason says what would fit.
674	
675	| What you tried | What the reason tells you |
676	| --- | --- |
677	| Setting an end rate too high | The largest end rate that fits, to 0.001. If no rate down to ×0.1 fits, it names the latest clip end that would fit at ×0.1. |
678	| Moving, resizing or removing a Speed action, or clearing its rate | The latest clip end that fits |
679	| Applying **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** | The largest rate that fits, or that no rate fits |
680	
681	Nothing changes when this happens. Frame Job beeps and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector, starting "Refused:". It stays there until you click it or the project changes. In the Speed Ramp sheet the reason appears in the [readout](/speed/make-a-ramp/#the-readout) and **Apply** is unavailable. Dragging a band doesn't show a reason. The band stays at the last place that fits.
682	
683	A clip end in a reason is a position on the timeline, given in ticks, Frame Job's own unit of time. Divide by 600,000 to get seconds. Trim the clip's end to that time and the ramp has enough file to play.
684	
685	## The rate line
686	
687	A white line across the action lane draws the clip's rate over its length, higher where it plays faster and lower where it plays slower.
688	
689	The line is scaled from the clip's own slowest rate to its fastest, so a gentle ramp draws as tall as a steep one. Use it to see the ramp's shape. For the figures, see the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/).
690	
691	The line shows at the **Medium** and **Large** track heights and in the Clip tab's lane. A clip whose rate never changes draws no line. While the line is drawn, a selected Speed band leaves out the curve it would otherwise show.
692	
693	The clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp too.
694	
695	## The band label
696	
697	At the **Large** track height, a Speed action's band on the timeline is labelled `speed`. A band's label lists everything its action changes, so one that also changes the clip's scale reads `scale, speed`. At **Medium** it shows only its number, and at **Small** it's a plain bar.
698	
699	## Good to know
700	
701	- A clip linked to its detached sound can't change its speed. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
702	- Going above ×12 anywhere in a ramp silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/#ramps-and-the-12-rule).
703	- Sound on a ramped clip is rendered in the background, so a clip can be briefly silent after you edit it. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
704	- Captions over a ramped clip follow the ramp. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
705

721	
722	**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** makes a whole [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) in one step. Pick a shape and a rate, and the sheet adds the Speed actions for you. The clip keeps its start and its length, and plays more or less of its file.
723

725	
726	## Make a ramp
727	
728	<Steps>
729	
730	1. Select one clip. **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** is available only when exactly one video or audio clip is selected. It has no keyboard shortcut.
731	
732	2. To ramp part of the clip, set an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside it first. See [The span](#the-span).
733	
734	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**.
735	
736	4. Choose a **Shape** and a **Rate**. For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, choose a **Hold** too.
737	
738	5. Read the [readout](#the-readout), then choose **Apply**.
739	
740	</Steps>
741	
742	<Shot
743	  name="13b-speed-ramp-sheet.sheet"
744	  alt="The Speed Ramp sheet, with Shape set to Speed Dip, Rate 0.5 beside a Presets menu, Curve set to Ease In Out and Hold set to 50%. The readout below says Speed Dip, the whole clip, from 00:00:00:00 to 00:00:05:07, then ×1 to ×0.5, held 2.63 s, back to ×1. Cancel and Apply sit at the foot, with the range ×0.1 to ×1000 to their left."
745	/>
746	
747	**Apply** adds the actions as one undo step named after the shape, such as **Speed Dip**. When captions move with it, the step's name adds "and Re-time Captions".
748	
749	The result is ordinary Speed actions, one for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down** and two for **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**. They show as bands on the action lane and you can [edit them by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/) like any other action.
750	
751	## The span
752	
753	The ramp covers the timeline's in/out range if that range lies entirely inside the clip. Otherwise it covers the whole clip, and an in/out range that runs past either edge of the clip is ignored.
754	
755	The [readout](#the-readout) says which one you've got.
756	
757	## The shapes
758	
759	| Shape | What it makes | Rate must be | Default rate |
760	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
761	| **Ramp Up** | One action over the span, rising from the current rate to your rate and holding it after. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |
762	| **Ramp Down** | One action over the span, falling to your rate and holding it after. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
763	| **Speed Dip** | Two actions: a ramp down to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Below the rate where the span starts | ×0.5 |
764	| **Speed Burst** | Two actions: a ramp up to your rate at the start of the span, a hold, and a ramp back to the starting rate at its end. | Above the rate where the span starts | ×2 |
765	
766	"Up" and "down" describe the rate where the span starts, not time. That rate is the clip's own rate, or the rate an earlier Speed action ended on, so a ramp can't start slow and rise to the clip's own rate. For that, set the clip to the slow rate first, then use **Ramp Up**.
767	
768	**Speed Dip** is the default because it plays less of the file, so it fits a clip that already uses its whole file. Anything that rises past the starting rate needs footage beyond the clip's current end. If a clip has none spare, trim its end first.
769	
770	## The controls
771	
772	| Control | What it does | Default |
773	| --- | --- | --- |
774	| **Shape** | One of the four shapes above. Choosing a shape resets **Rate** to that shape's default. | Speed Dip |
775	| **Rate** | The rate the ramp reaches, from ×0.1 to ×1000. **Presets** offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×, the same as the Speed sheet. | Set by **Shape**: ×0.5 for Speed Dip |
776	| **Curve** | How each new action eases: **Ease In Out** or **Linear**. | Ease In Out |
777	| **Hold** | For **Speed Dip** and **Speed Burst**, how much of the span stays at your rate: **None**, **25%**, **50%** or **75%**. Dimmed for **Ramp Up** and **Ramp Down**, which hold nothing. | 50% |
778	
779	The sheet opens on these defaults every time.
780	
781	With **Hold**, the rest of the span is split evenly between the two ramps, each rounded down to whole frames and at least one frame long. On a 6-second span at 50%, each ramp takes 1.5 s and the rate holds for 3 s. At **None** the two ramps meet.
782	
783	## The readout
784	
785	The sheet tries the ramp on every change, including each keystroke in **Rate**, and shows what it would make.
786	
787	The first line gives the shape and the span in timecode, such as `Speed Dip · the whole clip 00:00:02:00 – 00:00:08:00`. It says `the range` instead when the ramp covers the in/out range.
788	
789	The second line gives the rates, such as `×1 → ×0.5, held 3.00 s, → ×1`. If the ramp can't be made, the second line gives the reason instead and **Apply** is unavailable.
790	
791	## When Apply is unavailable
792	
793	Nothing changes in any of these cases. The readout gives the reason. It can quote clip and action ids, which aren't the numbers on the bands, and times in ticks, Frame Job's own unit of time, where 600,000 ticks make a second. The checks run in this order, so fixing one can show the next.
794	
795	| The problem | What to do |
796	| --- | --- |
797	| The span overlaps an action already on the clip. This counts any action, including one that would sit inside a dip's or burst's hold. The reason names it, and it's never replaced. | Set an in/out range clear of the action, or [move or remove](/speed/build-a-ramp/#move-and-resize-an-action) it. |
798	| A **Speed Dip** or **Speed Burst** span is shorter than two frames. | Widen the in/out range. |
799	| The rate is on the wrong side of the starting rate, such as a **Ramp Up** to a rate that isn't faster. | Change **Rate** or **Shape**. The reason gives the starting rate. |
800	| The clip is linked to its detached sound. | Choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
801	| The ramp would [play past the end of the file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file). | Use the largest rate that fits, which the reason names, or trim the clip's end. |
802	
803	## Good to know
804	
805	- Taking a clip with sound past ×12 asks once first, on the sheet. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the ramp, and **Cancel** leaves the sheet open. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
806	- Captions on a Captions track are re-timed in the same step. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
807	
808	## With an agent
809	
810	`add_speed_ramp` takes `clip`, `rate` and a `shape`: `ramp_up`, `ramp_down`, `speed_dip` or `speed_burst`. It isn't tied to the in/out range. Give `from` and `to` together, measured from the clip's start, to set the span, or neither for the whole clip. A span running past the clip's end isn't accepted, which can't happen from the sheet.
811	
812	It can also use any action curve and any `hold` from 0 to 0.9, and a larger hold comes down to 0.9. A `hold` on `ramp_up` or `ramp_down` is an error. So is a rate of zero or less, and any other rate outside ×0.1 to ×1000 is brought inside that range.
813	
814	The result gives the new actions' ids in `new_actions`, adds `audio_left_out` and `audio_note` when a clip goes past ×12, and adds `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` when captions moved. See [`add_speed_ramp`](/mcp/tools-speed/#add_speed_ramp).
815

2	title: "Build a ramp by hand"
3	description: "Add Speed actions yourself, set each one's rate and curve, and move, resize, split or remove them."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Building a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) by hand gives you full control of each change of speed, where it starts, how long it takes and how it eases. Use it when the four shapes in [Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) don't fit.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
14	  keys="⌥⌘K"
15	  where={['The action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Rate']}
16	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action', 'remove_action']}
17	/>
18	
19	## Build a ramp
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Select the clip and put the playhead where the change of speed should start.
24	
25	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>), or the **+** in the action lane's header. The new action is 1 s long, uses the **Linear** curve, and is selected.
26	
27	3. [Move or resize](#move-and-resize-an-action) its band so it covers the change, and [set its curve](#set-the-curve).
28	
29	4. In the Clip tab's **Speed** section, [set **Rate**](#set-the-rate) to the rate this action should end on.
30	
31	5. Repeat for each change of speed. Each action starts from the rate the last one ended on.
32	
33	</Steps>
34	
35	<Shot
36	  name="10d-clip-speed-action.inspector"
37	  alt="The Clip tab with an action selected. The action lane reads Actions 1, editing 1, with one green band, a white rate line rising across it, and a row below for the action's start, its length of 1.00 s, its curve set to Linear and a trash button. Further down, the Speed section shows Rate at 2.00× with now 1.50× in coral beside it, and a Clear button in its header."
38	/>
39	
40	**Add Action** is available when a selected clip is under the playhead. An action needs a full second free, so Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector if it would run past the clip's end or overlap another action. Move the playhead earlier, or clear the way.
41	
42	## Set the rate
43	
44	While an action is selected, the **Speed** section edits that action rather than the clip. **Rate** shows the rate the action ends on. Type a rate from ×0.1 to ×1000, or pick 0.50×, 1.00×, 2.00× or 4.00× from its menu. Doing this turns any action into a Speed action.
45	
46	If the action doesn't set a rate yet, **Rate** shows the rate the clip is playing at the end of that action. The coral **now** beside the field shows the rate at the playhead, when that differs. There's no **Reset** while an action is selected, so to end the action at ×1, enter 1.
47	
48	To take the rate out of an action and keep the action, choose **Clear** in the section header. This is one undo step, and it can't be done if the clip would then [play past the end of its file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file). See [Clear a rate from an action](/speed/speed-section/#clear-a-rate-from-an-action) for the other ways to do it.
49	
50	**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** still belong to the clip, so their rows are marked ⊘. A length typed in **Fit to** changes the clip, not the action. See [Rows that stay the clip's](/speed/speed-section/#rows-that-stay-the-clips).
51	
52	A rate too high for the file isn't accepted, and the reason at the foot of the inspector names the largest that fits. Setting a rate above ×12 on a clip with sound [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
53	
54	## Set the curve
55	
56	The curve is how an action eases from its starting rate to its end rate. Select the action and choose from the curve pop-up in the detail row under the Clip tab's action lane. It has no label of its own, and shows the curve's name:
57	
58	| Curve | How the rate moves |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| **Linear** | Steadily, from start to end. This is what a new action uses. |
61	| **In** | Slowly at first. |
62	| **Out** | Slowly at the end. |
63	| **In Out** | Slowly at both ends. |
64	
65	Changing a curve changes how much of the file the ramp plays, so a change won't go through if the ramp would then play past the end of the file. The undo step is **Action Curve**.
66	
67	## Move and resize an action
68	
69	Drag the middle of a band on the action lane to move it. Drag either end to resize it. The grips are the outer 5 pt of a band, and they show when you hover over a band wider than 15 pt.
70	
71	Bands drag the same way on the timeline and in the Clip tab's lane. A drag snaps to whole frames and stops at the next action and at the clip's end. An action can't be shorter than one frame.
72	
73	You can also type in the detail row: the first field is where the action starts, measured from the clip's start, and the second is its length.
74	
75	The undo steps are **Move Action** and **Resize Action**. Captions over the clip move in the same step, which adds "and Re-time Captions" to the name. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
76	
77	Moving or resizing a Speed action changes how much of the file the clip plays. If a drag would take the clip past the end of its file, the band stays at the last place that fits. If a typed value would, nothing changes and the reason names the latest clip end that fits.
78	
79	## The playhead selects the action
80	
81	With one clip selected, playing or scrubbing into an action selects it. The Speed section then edits that action. Clicking a band also selects it, and parks the playhead at the action's end so the preview shows the rate you're setting.
82	
83	An action stays selected when the playhead moves out of it, until the playhead enters another action or you go back to the clip. So check the lane's header before you change **Rate**. It reads "editing" and the action's number while an action is selected.
84	
85	## Back to editing the clip
86	
87	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or choose the **Clip** chip at the left of the Clip tab's action lane. The Speed section edits the clip itself again.
88	
89	The playhead can stay inside the action, and it won't be selected again until the playhead leaves and comes back.
90	
91	## Remove an action
92	
93	Select the action and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>, or choose the trash button in the detail row. With an action selected, <kbd>⌫</kbd> removes the action and not the clip. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
94	
95	A Speed action can't be removed if the clip would then play past the end of its file, which happens when the action was slowing the clip down. The reason at the foot of the inspector names the latest clip end that fits.
96	
97	The undo step is **Remove Action**, or **Remove Action and Re-time Captions** when captions move.
98	
99	## Split inside an action
100	
101	To [split a clip](/editing/splitting/) partway through a Speed action, put the playhead inside the action and split as usual. The split keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. Each half gets its own Speed action, and the second half starts at the rate the clip had reached.
102	
103	Two things can change, depending on the curve:
104	
105	- With **Out** or **In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
106	- With **In** or **In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file.
107	
108	See [Split inside a Speed action](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/#split-inside-a-speed-action) for how the rates are worked out.
109	
110	## Good to know
111	
112	A clip linked to its detached sound can't have its Speed actions changed until you choose [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
113	
114	## With an agent
115	
116	`add_action` adds the action, and `set_action_end` with `speed` in its `patch`, such as `{ "speed": 3 }`, sets the rate it ends on. `speed: null` takes the rate out again. `set_action` moves or resizes an action and sets its curve, and `remove_action` removes it. See [Speed in an action](/mcp/tools-animation/#speed-in-an-action).

126	title: Edit a ramped clip
127	description: What a speed change, trim, split or freeze frame does to a clip with a speed ramp, and why Frame Job sometimes won't make the edit.
128	---
129	
130	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
131	
132	Once a clip has a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), your ordinary edits still work on it. This page says what each one does to the ramp, and what stops an edit that would break it.
133	
134	<AtAGlance
135	  menu="Clip ▸ Speed…"
136	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge', 'The action lane']}
137	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'set_action']}
138	/>
139	
140	## Scale a whole ramp
141	
142	These all change a ramped clip's speed by scaling the whole ramp by one factor:
143	
144	- **Clip ▸ Speed…**
145	- **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/), with no action selected
146	- **Fit to** in the Speed section
147	- The ⌥ [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) on the clip's end edge
148	- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), for the part of the clip inside the range
149	
150	The clip's own rate, every end rate and the length of every Speed action scale together, so the ramp keeps its shape and the clip still plays the same stretch of its file. The clip itself gets shorter or longer. A ramp from ×1 to ×2 scaled by ×2 becomes a ramp from ×2 to ×4, in half the time. With a ramped clip selected, the Speed sheet's readout ends "Each speed ramp keeps its shape: the rates it names scale with the base rate."
151	
152	No rate in a clip can go below ×0.1 or above ×1000, and what happens at those limits depends on how you made the change:
153	
154	| You used | At a limit |
155	| --- | --- |
156	| **Speed…**, **Rate** or **Fit to** | Scaling stops at the limit, so the clip's rate can end up short of the rate you asked for. |
157	| The ⌥ rate stretch | The clip stops following the drag at the last length inside the limits. |
158	| Retime Range | Frame Job won't make the edit, and the reason names the clip and the rate. |
159	
160	To change one rate inside the ramp instead, select its action. **Rate** then sets that action's end rate. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
161	
162	## Edits follow the ramp
163	
164	Trims, slips, rolls, splits, freeze frames and transitions all read the ramp, so each cut or held frame is the frame the ramp actually plays at that moment.
165	
166	| Edit | What it does on a ramped clip |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| [Trim](/editing/trimming/) the start | The frame under the edge stays put. The Speed actions stay the same distance from the clip's start, so what plays after the new start can change. The edge stops where the clip would otherwise play past the end of its file. |
169	| Trim the end | The Speed actions don't move. How far you can pull the end out depends on the rate the clip reaches, not on its own rate. |
170	| [Roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) | The later clip's start behaves as a start trim, and the earlier clip's end as an end trim. |
171	| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) | The source moves at the clip's own rate, and the Speed actions stay where they are. It stops so the clip never plays past the end of its file. |
172	| [Split](#split-inside-a-speed-action) | The two halves meet at the frame the ramp plays at the cut, and the second half starts at the rate playing there. |
173	| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | The still holds the frame the ramp plays at that moment. |
174	| [Transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) | The overlap follows the ramp. The earlier clip carries on past its old end, and the extra footage before the later clip's start plays at that clip's own rate. The later clip still ends on the same frame of its file. |
175	| [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | The separate audio clip gets the same ramp. |
176	
177	[**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**](/editing/paste-attributes/) never copies a speed or a ramp.
178	
179	Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it. Captions already on the timeline [follow a later change to the ramp](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
180	
181	## Split inside a Speed action
182	
183	Splitting partway through a Speed action keeps the picture continuous at the cut, with no repeated or skipped frame. The action becomes two, one on each half. The first ends at whatever rate makes the picture meet at the cut, and the second keeps the original end rate.
184	
185	The action's curve matters here:
186	
187	- With **Out** or **In Out**, the rate can jump at the cut.
188	- With **In** or **In Out**, the second half can end on a different frame of the file than the unsplit clip did. If it would then play past the end of the file, its end rate is lowered to the largest that fits.
189	
190	## Filmstrip and waveform
191	
192	A ramped clip's filmstrip and waveform follow the ramp, so what you see at a point on the timeline is what plays there. A stretch at a high rate shows more of the file in the same space.
193	
194	## An action past the clip's end
195	
196	After a trim, or after a ramp is scaled, a Speed action can lie partly or wholly past the clip's end. It stays on the clip, and you can still change its curve, move it earlier or shorten it. Being past the end stops only a change that takes it further past.
197	
198	Its end rate still counts for the [×12 rule](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), even though that part never plays. If a clip is silent though it never seems to pass ×12, look for an action like this.
199	
200	## When a ramp edit can't be made
201	
202	A ramped clip keeps its place and its length on the timeline, so a ramp can't play past the end of the clip's file. Frame Job won't make an edit that would, and the reason says what would fit: the largest rate, or the latest clip end. [Never past the end of the file](/speed/speed-ramps/#never-past-the-end-of-the-file) lists what each edit names.
203	
204	**Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** has a few more conditions, such as a span that overlaps another action. See [When Apply is unavailable](/speed/make-a-ramp/#when-apply-is-unavailable).
205	
206	A clip with [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) is linked to its audio, so no speed or ramp edit will change it. The reason says to use Attach Audio first.
207	
208	Whatever stops the edit, nothing changes. Frame Job beeps, makes no undo step, and shows the reason:
209	
210	- **At the foot of the inspector**, after the word "Refused:". It stays until the project changes or you click it. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
211	- **In the Speed Ramp sheet's readout**, as you adjust the sheet, so nothing has been applied and there's no beep. **Apply** is dimmed until the preset fits.
212	
213	Dragging an action's band is different. There's no beep and no reason, and the band stays at the last place that worked.
214	
215	A reason can give a time in ticks, the unit Frame Job counts time in. There are 600,000 ticks in a second, so 1,200,000 ticks is 2 seconds.

226	title: Sound on a ramp
227	description: How Frame Job renders the sound of a ramped clip in the background, why the clip goes silent for a moment, and what an export does about it.
228	---
229	
230	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
231	
232	A clip whose speed changes as it plays can't play its sound straight from the file, so Frame Job renders that sound in the background. While it renders, the clip is silent in the preview. An export always waits for it.
233	
234	<AtAGlance
235	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section ▸ Keep pitch"
236	  tools={['set_speed', 'export']}
237	/>
238	
239	## Rendered audio
240	
241	Two kinds of clip have their sound rendered into a separate file:
242	
243	- a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), with **Keep pitch** on or off
244	- a clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off
245	
246	A clip at a constant speed with **Keep pitch** on isn't rendered, and neither is a clip above ×12, because [it has no sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
247	
248	There's nothing to start. A new render begins after each edit that changes the clip's timing, such as a ramp, its rate, a trim or a split, and after you change **Keep pitch**. During a drag, it waits until you let go.
249	
250	Each render covers the whole clip's sound, so how long it takes grows with the clip's length and rate. Renders run one at a time, in the background, so you can keep editing. An edit that makes a render out of date drops it, so a run of quick edits doesn't queue up work.
251	
252	The files are saved inside the project package, in `cache/ramp-audio/`, and Frame Job can rebuild them. Until a new project is saved, they're in a temporary folder. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) doesn't copy them, so the new project renders its own.
253	
254	## Keep pitch off
255	
256	The sound glides smoothly up and down in pitch with the rate, like tape, and stays in step with the picture. At a constant speed it plays at that speed's tape pitch.
257	
258	## Keep pitch on
259	
260	The sound keeps its own pitch as the speed changes. After a steep slow-down, such as ×2 to ×0.5, it can run up to about 24 ms behind the picture.
261	
262	See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) for the control itself.
263	
264	## Silent while it renders
265	
266	While a clip's sound is rendering, that clip plays silent in the preview. Everything else on the timeline plays as usual, and the clip's sound comes back on its own when the render finishes.
267	
268	## Undo and redo render again
269	
270	Undo and redo usually start a render too, because Frame Job drops the file from before the edit once a newer render lands. The clip is briefly silent then as well.
271	
272	## Exports wait for it
273	
274	An export waits for every render it needs and never writes that sound silent. The Exporting sheet reads "Preparing “*name*”…" during the wait, and a queued export's row reads `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel either one there. This covers speed ramps and clips at a constant speed other than ×1 with **Keep pitch** off.
275	
276	An animated GIF or APNG has no sound, so it doesn't wait. An export an agent starts with `export` waits the same way.
277	
278	## A failed render
279	
280	If a render fails, an export that needs it stops with this message, naming the clip:
281	
282	> Clip N's retimed audio could not be rendered: …
283	
284	Frame Job doesn't try a failed render again while it stays open. The clip stays silent, and exports that need it keep failing, until you change the clip's timing, which starts a new render, or quit and reopen Frame Job.
285

299	
300	When you change the speed of a clip with sound, the captions over it move with its speech, so they stay on the words you hear. There's nothing to turn on.
301	
302	<AtAGlance
303	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…']}
304	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Speed section', 'The action lane', '⌥-drag a clip\'s end edge']}
305	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
306	/>
307	
308	## What moves them
309	
310	Captions move when you:
311	
312	- change the clip's speed, with **Clip ▸ Speed…**, the Speed section or the ⌥ rate stretch
313	- add a ramp with **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…**
314	- add, move, resize, edit or remove a Speed action on the clip
315	
316	The captions move in the same undo step as the edit, so one undo puts them back too. The step is named after the edit with "and Re-time Captions" added, such as **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**. A drag moves them when you let go of the mouse.
317	
318	The clip has to be one captions could have been made from: it plays media with sound, its audio is on, and it isn't reversed.
319	
320	## Which captions move
321	
322	A caption moves when all of these are true:
323	
324	- It's a text clip on a track named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**.
325	- That track holds only text clips and isn't locked.
326	- It lies wholly inside the clip you edited.
327	
328	A caption that runs past either edge of the clip stays where it is, and so does anything on another track.
329	
330	## Speech the clip no longer plays
331	
332	A ramp that slows a clip down makes it play less of its file, so it can stop reaching speech it played before.
333	
334	A caption whose speech the clip no longer reaches is removed. A word caption page that's only partly reached keeps the words that still play, and its text is cut to match.
335	
336	## Newly revealed speech
337	
338	When a ramp makes the clip play further into its file, the new part gets no captions. [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) again to caption it.
339	
340	## Neighbouring captions
341	
342	A moved caption is cut back where it would run into a caption that didn't move. One that would start inside such a caption, or end up shorter than a frame, is removed.
343	
344	## Good to know
345	
346	- Only speed and ramp edits re-time captions. A trim, slip or split leaves them where they are.
347	- [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) works differently. It stretches or squeezes a text clip in the range along with everything else, and Frame Job won't retime a range that touches a caption page with timed words.
348	- Frame Job checks every caption's new place before it makes the edit. If they don't all work out, the speed edit goes through on its own and the captions stay where they were.
349	
350	## With an agent
351	
352	`set_speed`, `rate_stretch`, `add_speed_ramp`, `set_action`, `remove_action` and `set_action_end` re-time captions the same way, in the same undo step. `set_action_end` does so only when it changes the speed.
353	
354	The result lists the caption clips that moved in `captions_retimed` and the ones removed in `captions_removed`. Each key appears only when it has something in it. See [Captions move with the speech](/mcp/tools-speed/#captions-move-with-the-speech) and [`set_action`](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action).
355

364	title: Retime Range
365	description: Play the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and keep everything after it in step.
366	---
367	
368	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
369	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
370	
371	Retime Range plays the stretch between In and Out faster or slower on every unlocked track at once, and moves everything after Out up or back to stay in step. Use it to speed up a slow part of a screen recording with its microphone and camera together.
372	
373	<AtAGlance
374	  menu="Clip ▸ Retime Range…"
375	  tools="retime_range"
376	  needs="An in/out range."
377	/>
378	
379	## Retime a range
380	
381	<Steps>
382	
383	1. Set [In and Out](/timeline/in-out-range/) around the stretch. The menu item is dimmed without them, and while another sheet is open.
384	
385	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Retime Range…**, right after **Close Gap**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
386	
387	3. Set the **Rate**, and tick or untick **Preserve pitch**.
388	
389	4. Choose **Apply**.
390	
391	</Steps>
392	
393	The whole edit is one undo step, **Retime Range**.
394	
395	## The sheet
396	
397	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
398	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
399	| **Rate:** | How much faster the range plays. ×2 makes it half as long, and ×0.5 twice as long. The **Presets** pull-down offers 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× and 100×. | ×2 | ×0.1 to ×1000 |
400	| **Preserve pitch** | Sets the pitch setting on every video or audio clip in the range, as [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) does on one clip. | As the first video or audio clip on an unlocked track in the range has it, or on when there is none | |
401	
402	**Apply** at ×1 closes the sheet and changes nothing. At any other rate it retimes the range.
403	
404	If the rate takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job [asks first](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/), because above ×12 a clip's audio is left out. **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the edit. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed.
405	
406	## What happens in the range
407	
408	The range gets shorter or longer by the rate, and everything after Out moves to match. A 10 s range at ×2 lasts 5 s, and what follows it starts 5 s earlier.
409	
410	### Clips across an edge
411	
412	A clip that crosses In or Out is cut there first, as [Split](/editing/splitting/) cuts it. Only the piece inside the range changes speed.
413	
414	### Rates multiply
415	
416	Each video or audio clip inside plays at its own rate times the **Rate**, so a ×2 clip retimed by ×2 plays at ×4. A [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/#scale-a-whole-ramp) keeps its shape, and every rate in it scales.
417	
418	### Titles, shapes and stills
419	
420	Titles, shapes, stills, images, graphics and adjustment clips inside are stretched or squeezed by the same amount. A graphic with a length of its own keeps it.
421	
422	### Actions
423	
424	Actions keep their place in each clip, at the same fraction of its length. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
425	
426	### Markers and detached sound
427	
428	Markers inside the range move with the picture, and markers after it move with everything else. A detached sound linked to a moved clip moves with it.
429	
430	## Inside a nest
431	
432	Retime Range works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), where it retimes the nest's own tracks and uses the nest's own In and Out. A nest has no markers of its own, so none moves.
433	
434	## When a range can't be retimed
435	
436	Nothing changes, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Frame Job stops at the first problem it finds, working roughly in this order, so fixing one can show the next:
437	
438	| What stops it | What to do |
439	| --- | --- |
440	| The rate is outside ×0.1 to ×1000. | This only comes up with an agent, because the sheet's field stays inside this range. |
441	| The range is under two frames. | Widen the range. |
442	| A locked track has a clip that ends after In. It would fall out of step. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), or move In past that clip. |
443	| The range touches a nest clip. | Move the range off it, or retime inside the nest. |
444	| The range touches a caption page with timed words. | Move the range off it. |
445	| The range touches half of a linked pair. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
446	| A transition touches the range. | Move the range off it, or remove the transition. |
447	| Two markers would land on the same time. | Move one of them first. |
448	| A clip would play faster than ×1000 or slower than ×0.1. The message names the clip and the rate. | Pick a gentler rate, or set the clip's own speed first. |
449	| A clip would be squeezed under one frame. The message names it. | Pick a gentler rate. |
450	
451	A clip only has to overlap the range to count, so a nest or a linked clip that crosses In or Out stops the edit too.
452	
453	## With an agent
454	
455	`retime_range` makes the same edit, but it takes the range as times, `from` and `to`, so it needs no In and Out. It also needs a `rate`, and a rate of 1 changes nothing. `keep_pitch` is optional, and without it each clip keeps the setting it has.
456	
457	The result lists the pieces the cuts made in `new_clips`. It never asks about ×12: the clip's audio is left out, and the result carries `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/#retime_range).
458

466	title: Reverse a clip
467	description: Play a clip back to front, picture and sound, and deal with the backwards copy Frame Job renders to do it.
468	---
469	
470	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
471	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
472	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
473	
474	Reverse plays a clip back to front, picture and sound together. The Mac's playback can't run video backwards, so the first time you reverse a file, Frame Job renders a backwards copy of it and the clip plays from that.
475	
476	<AtAGlance
477	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Timing"
478	  tools="set_reversed"
479	/>
480	
481	<Shot
482	  name="10-clip-clip-tab.inspector"
483	  alt="The Clip tab on its Clip sub-tab, with the Timing section open: In, Out and Duration, then an unticked Reverse checkbox, Reversed frames reading a dash, and a dimmed Render Reverse button."
484	/>
485	
486	## Reverse a clip
487	
488	<Steps>
489	
490	1. Select the clip, or several clips.
491	
492	2. In the inspector, go to the **Clip** tab and its **Clip** sub-tab, and open **Timing** if it's closed.
493	
494	3. Tick **Reverse**.
495	
496	</Steps>
497	
498	If the file has no backwards copy yet, the [Reversing sheet](#the-reversing-sheet) appears while Frame Job makes one. When it closes, the clip plays backwards. If a copy already exists, the clip plays backwards straight away.
499	
500	Untick **Reverse** to play the clip forwards again. Each change is one undo step, called **Reverse**.
501	
502	## Where Reverse lives
503	
504	Reverse is for clips of a video or audio file. Text, shapes, graphics, adjustment clips, nests, pictures and freeze frames have no Reverse rows.
505	
506	With one clip selected, **Timing** shows [In, Out and Duration](/editing/timing-section/) above the Reverse rows. With several clips of video or audio files selected, it shows only the Reverse rows, and the section's summary is their total length.
507	
508	| Row | What it does |
509	| --- | --- |
510	| **Reverse** | Plays the clip back to front, or forwards again. |
511	| **Reversed frames** | Shows the state of the [backwards copy](#reversed-frames). |
512	| **Render Reverse** | Starts a stopped or failed render [again](#render-reverse). |
513	
514	With several clips selected, **Reverse** applies to all of them as one undo step. If they disagree, the row is tagged `mixed` and the box shows the first clip's state. Clicking it then sets every clip the same way.
515	
516	## Reversed frames
517	
518	This row tells you where the backwards copy has got to.
519	
520	| It reads | What it means |
521	| --- | --- |
522	| — | The clip isn't reversed. |
523	| Rendering… | The copy is being made, or is about to be. |
524	| Rendered | The copy exists and the clip plays from it. |
525	| Not rendered | The render was cancelled or failed. **Render Reverse** is available. |
526	| Media missing | The clip's file is missing or has no length. |
527	
528	Across several clips, the row shows the state that needs attention first: Not rendered, then Rendering…, Media missing, Rendered.
529	
530	## The Reversing sheet
531	
532	The sheet appears when a reversed clip needs a copy that doesn't exist, unless that file's render was cancelled or failed. Ticking **Reverse** is the usual reason. Opening a project whose package has lost its `cache` folder is another.
533	
534	It shows a progress bar, the line "Rendering a reversed copy of “name”…" or "Rendering reversed copies of 3 files…", and the name of the file being worked on. When it finishes, the sheet closes and the clip plays backwards.
535	
536	Editing commands are unavailable while the sheet is up. If an agent reverses another clip in the meantime, that clip's render starts when the sheet closes.
537	
538	### Cancel the render
539	
540	Choose **Cancel**. The sheet reads "Stopping…" until the render has stopped, then says:
541	
542	> Stopped. Clips that are still reversed show a slate until their frames are rendered — press Render Reverse in the Timing section of the Clip tab to try again.
543	
544	Choose **Close** to carry on. Files that had already finished are kept, and the clip stays reversed.
545	
546	### When a file can't be reversed
547	
548	The sheet says how many files failed, for example "2 files could not be reversed. Those clips show a slate rather than play forwards." Below that it names the first file and the reason. Choose **Close** to carry on. Files that rendered are kept.
549	
550	## The slate
551	
552	Until a clip's copy exists, it shows a slate instead of playing forwards: a dark plate with diagonal stripes, in the clip's place on the canvas. The clip plays no sound either. A clip with no picture stays silent and draws nothing.
553	
554	:::caution
555	An export made while a clip shows a slate writes the slate. Finish the render first.
556	:::
557	
558	## Render Reverse
559	
560	Nothing restarts a stopped render by itself. **Render Reverse** is how you try again, and it's available only when **Reversed frames** reads Not rendered.
561	
562	Each press renders one file, shared by every reversed clip of that file. If several files are waiting, press it once for each file until no selected clip reads Not rendered.
563	
564	Unticking **Reverse** on every clip of a file and ticking it again also starts a new render.
565	
566	## The clip stays in place
567	
568	Reversing never moves a clip. It keeps its start, its length and its in point.
569	
570	The in point is counted in the direction the clip plays, so reversing a trimmed clip shows the other end of the file. Take a 10 s file trimmed to its first 3 s. Reversed, the clip plays the file's last 3 s, from 10 s back to 7 s. To play a different part, [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) the clip.
571	
572	## Reverse with speed and ramps
573	
574	Reverse works with [Speed](/speed/change-speed/), [Fit to](/speed/fit-to-duration/), the [⌥ rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) and [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/). The in point and the ramp both count in the direction the clip plays, so a reversed ramped clip ramps through the file backwards.
575	
576	## The backwards copy
577	
578	Frame Job renders one copy per file. It's kept in the [project package](/reference/framejob-package/)'s `cache` folder with the other things Frame Job can rebuild, and every reversed clip of that file shares it. The same file can play forwards on one clip and backwards on another.
579	
580	The copy stays after you untick **Reverse**, so ticking it again doesn't render anything. [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) brings the copies its clips play along with it.
581	
582	The copy belongs to one version of the file, in one place. If the file changes or moves, or you [relink](/projects/relink-media/) the clip to another file, Frame Job renders a new copy and removes the old one.
583	
584	## Depth and colour
585	
586	The copy is rendered at 10 bits, at the source's exact size, with the colour information from the source file, so an HDR or log clip still looks right when reversed. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
587	
588	It's written as HEVC Main 10. A source with an odd width or height takes ProRes 422 instead, which makes a file several times larger.
589	
590	:::caution
591	The copy doesn't keep an alpha channel. A reversed ProRes 4444 clip loses its transparency.
592	:::
593	
594	## Good to know
595	
596	### Still images
597	
598	A picture on the timeline looks the same backwards, so it has no Reverse rows and nothing to render. The same goes for a [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/).
599	
600	### Linked clips
601	
602	Frame Job won't reverse a clip linked to its detached sound. The foot of the inspector says which clips are linked. Choose **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (<kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>) first. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). With several clips selected, the others still reverse.
603	
604	### Commands that need a forward clip
605	
606	- [Generate Captions](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/) skips a reversed clip, because its words would come out backwards.
607	- [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [Add Shortcut Overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) won't work on one.
608	
609	## With an agent
610	
611	`set_reversed` takes the clip and `reversed`, true or false, so it says which way to play and isn't a toggle. The Reversing sheet appears in the project's window, as it does when you tick **Reverse**, and the clip shows the [slate](#the-slate) until the copy exists. See [`set_reversed`](/mcp/tools-speed/#set_reversed).
612

621	title: Freeze frame
622	description: Hold the frame under the playhead for 2 seconds, keep the rest of the cut in sync, and choose which frame the still holds.
623	---
624	
625	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
626	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
627	
628	Freeze Frame holds one moment of a clip on screen for 2 s, then lets the clip carry on. Use it to pause on a reaction, or to give a title or a voice-over time to land.
629	
630	<AtAGlance
631	  menu="Clip ▸ Freeze Frame"
632	  keys="⇧⌘F"
633	  tools={['freeze_frame', 'slip']}
634	/>
635	
636	## Freeze a frame
637	
638	<Steps>
639	
640	1. Select the clip.
641	
642	2. Move the playhead to the frame you want to hold.
643	
644	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame**, or press <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd>.
645	
646	</Steps>
647	
648	Frame Job splits the clip at the playhead, opens 2 s of empty time there, and fills the gap on the clip's track with a still of that source frame. The rest of the clip picks up after the still. All of this is one undo step, called **Freeze Frame**.
649	
650	The still has no sound, so the clip's own sound stops for the hold.
651	
652	If the playhead sits on the clip's first frame, there's nothing to cut. The still goes in and the whole clip moves after it.
653	
654	## When it is available
655	
656	Freeze Frame works on a selected clip under the playhead. With nothing selected there, it's dimmed. A playhead exactly at a clip's end isn't on that clip. With several selected clips under the playhead, it acts on the first.
657	
658	It needs a clip of a video file with its picture. An audio-only clip, text, a shape, a picture, a graphic, an adjustment clip, a nest or another still can't be frozen. The command stays available on those, and Frame Job shows an error saying the clip "is not a media clip" or "has no video properties". Nothing changes.
659	
660	## Everything stays in sync
661	
662	The 2 s opens across every unlocked track, so the cut stays together:
663	
664	- Clips that start at or after the playhead move 2 s later, on every unlocked track.
665	- Markers at or after the playhead move with them.
666	- A clip on another track that crosses the playhead is neither cut nor moved. It plays on through the hold, as a music bed would.
667	- Sound [linked](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to the frozen clip is cut at the playhead too, and its second half moves with the picture.
668	- Clips on locked tracks stay where they are.
669	
670	## The still keeps the clip's look
671	
672	The still keeps the clip's position, scale, crop and other picture settings as they were at that moment, including any action that was moving it. It lines up with the frame it froze, so the hold doesn't jump.
673	
674	The still has no actions of its own: its look at that moment is written into its own properties. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
675	
676	A [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) isn't carried over, so the still doesn't arrive or depart again. Freeze partway through an arrival and the still sits where the clip belongs, without the preset's movement, so the picture jumps there.
677	
678	## Change the frozen frame
679	
680	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the still's body. The still stays where it is and holds an earlier frame of the source as you drag left, or a later one as you drag right. It stops at the first and last frames of the file. This is a [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/), one undo step called **Slip**.
681	
682	## Change how long it holds
683	
684	The hold is always 2 s from the menu. [Trim](/editing/trimming/) the still's end to change it. A trim moves only that edge, so shortening the still leaves a gap after it, which [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) removes.
685	
686	A still has no file end to stop it, so it can hold as long as you like, but the rest of the clip sits right behind it. To hold for longer, [open room](/editing/close-gaps/#open-room-by-hand) after the still first, then drag its end out. Pulled over the next clip instead, it makes an [overlap](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) with a Cross Dissolve.
687	
688	## On a ramped clip
689	
690	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) or a changed speed, the still holds the frame actually playing at the playhead.
691	
692	A [reversed](/speed/reverse/) clip is different. The still counts forwards through the file, so it usually holds another frame from the one on screen. [Drag it](#change-the-frozen-frame) to the frame you want.
693	
694	## Good to know
695	
696	Frame Job won't freeze where the still would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). It beeps, the foot of the inspector says why, and nothing changes. Two places do this:
697	
698	- Inside a [transition](/motion/transitions/), where the two clips already overlap.
699	- On a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/), because the rest of that track can't move out of the still's way.
700	
701	## With an agent
702	
703	`freeze_frame` takes the clip, an optional `at` (the playhead if left out) and an optional `duration` (2 s if left out), so it can hold any moment of a clip without moving the playhead, for any length of at least one frame. An `at` outside the clip or a shorter `duration` is an error. `slip` on a freeze frame moves the frame it holds. See [`freeze_frame`](/mcp/tools-speed/#freeze_frame).
704

3	description: "The ways to change a clip's time in Frame Job, which clips each one works on, and the rate and sound limits that apply."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Frame Job can play a video or audio clip faster or slower, change its speed over time, play it backwards and hold one of its frames. This page shows which tool fits the job and what limits apply to all of them.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Speed…', 'Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…', 'Clip ▸ Retime Range…']}
12	  keys="⌥-drag"
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Speed section"
14	  tools={['set_speed', 'rate_stretch', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Pick the right tool
18	
19	| You want to | Use | What happens on the timeline |
20	| --- | --- | --- |
21	| Play a clip at one new speed | [Clip ▸ Speed…](/speed/change-speed/) or **Rate** in the [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/) | The clip's start stays and its length changes. Later clips don't move. |
22	| Make a clip last an exact length | [Fit to](/speed/fit-to-duration/) | The rate changes so the clip plays in the length you type. |
23	| Stretch a clip by eye | [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dragging its end edge | The clip gets longer or shorter and still plays the same source. |
24	| Speed up and slow down inside a clip | A [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) | The clip keeps its place and length, and plays more or less of its file. |
25	| Speed up or slow down a stretch of the whole timeline | [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Every unlocked track changes together, and what follows moves up or back. |
26	| Speed up the typing in a screen recording | [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) | Only the stretches of typing change. |
27	| Play a clip backwards | [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) | Nothing on the timeline moves. |
28	| Hold one frame still | [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) | A still clip fills a gap opened at the playhead. |
29	
30	A rate is a multiple of normal speed: ×1 is normal, ×2 is twice as fast and half as long, and ×0.5 is half speed.
31	
32	Sound follows the [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) setting, which is on for a new clip.
33	
34	## Which clips take speed
35	
36	Speed works on **media clips**, meaning clips of a video or audio file. Other clips have no source to speed up. Retime Range is the one exception.
37	
38	| Clip | Speed…, Fit to, rate stretch, Speed Ramp…, Reverse and Freeze Frame | Retime Range… |
39	| --- | --- | --- |
40	| A video or audio file | Yes, but Freeze Frame needs a picture | Yes |
41	| A still image, a freeze frame, text, a shape or an adjustment clip | No | Stretched or squeezed with the range |
42	| A graphic | No. Its timing comes from its module and its **Length**. | Stretched or squeezed, and it keeps its **Length** |
43	| A nest | No | Frame Job won't retime a range with a nest in it. Move the range off the nest, or retime inside it. |
44	| A caption page with timed words | No | Frame Job won't retime a range with one in it. Move the range off it. |
45	
46	When a selection mixes clip kinds, each command treats it differently:
47	
48	- **Clip ▸ Speed…** is available when the selection holds at least one media clip. It opens on those clips and skips the rest. With none selected it's dimmed.
49	- **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** is available only with exactly one media clip selected.
50	- The **Speed** section appears only when every selected clip is a media clip.
51	- With several clips selected, the **Timing** section, which holds **Reverse**, also appears only when every one is a media clip.
52	- <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dragging the end edge of any other clip is an ordinary trim.
53	
54	### Linked clips
55	
56	After [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/), a picture and its sound are linked. Frame Job won't change a linked clip's rate or direction, or give it a Speed action, until you attach it again. The foot of the inspector shows the reason, for example "clip 4 is linked to clip 7: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". A rate stretch on a linked clip doesn't move and shows no reason.
57	
58	**Keep pitch** isn't a rate, so you can still change it on a linked clip.
59	
60	## Rate range
61	
62	A clip can play anywhere from ×0.1 to ×1000. What happens when you ask for more depends on where you ask.
63	
64	| Where | A rate past a limit |
65	| --- | --- |
66	| The **Speed**, **Speed Ramp** and **Retime Range** sheets | The field won't take it. Each sheet prints ×0.1 – ×1000 beside its buttons. |
67	| **Rate** in the Speed section | It's set to the nearest limit. |
68	| **Fit to** | The rate stops at the limit, so the clip ends up a different length from the one you typed. |
69	| A rate stretch | The clip stops following the drag at the last length inside the limits. |
70	
71	## Limits at a glance
72	
73	| Limit | Value |
74	| --- | --- |
75	| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
76	| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
77	| Fastest rate that still has sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
78	| Freeze frame length when none is given | 2 s |
79	
80	What else to expect:
81	
82	- **Above ×12** the picture plays and the sound is left out of the preview and the export. Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
83	- **On a ramped clip**, one rate above ×12 anywhere in the ramp silences the whole clip.
84	- **A speed ramp** never changes the clip's start or length. Frame Job won't make an edit that would play the clip past the end of its file.
85	- **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** works on one clip at a time, and offers the **Ease In Out** and **Linear** curves and four hold values.
86	- **Rendered sound.** A ramp is silent in the preview until its sound has been rendered. So is a clip at any constant speed but ×1 with Keep pitch off. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/#tape-pitch-is-rendered-in-the-background) and [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).
87	- **After a steep slow-down** with Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms.
88	- **A reversed clip** shows a slate until its backwards copy has been rendered.
89	- **Synchronize Audio** doesn't take clips that are reversed, ramped, or more than 0.2% away from ×1. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
90	
91	## With an agent
92	
93	`set_speed`, `add_speed_ramp` and a speed in `set_action_end` bring a rate past a limit to that limit. `retime_range` is the exception: it won't take a rate outside ×0.1 to ×1000. `set_speed`, `add_speed_ramp` and `retime_range` don't accept a rate of zero or less.
94	
95	Asking for a speed on anything but a media clip is an error, "clip 12 is not a media clip", so the agent can correct the call.
96	
97	`add_speed_ramp` can also use any action curve and any hold from 0 to 0.9, which is more than the sheet offers. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

142	## The Speed sheet
143	
144	<Shot

149	| Control | What it does | Default |

It takes up to three decimal places, and the field won't accept a value outside ×0.1 – ×1000, the range printed beside the sheet's buttons. | The rate the selected clips share, or ×1 if they differ |
152	| **Presets** | Fills in **Rate** with 0.25×, 0.50×, 1×, 1.5×, 2×, 4×, 10× or 100×. The same list appears on the [Speed Ramp](/speed/make-a-ramp/) and [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) sheets. | |

154	
155	## The readout
156	
157	Frame Job tries the change before you commit to it, so the readout shows what **Apply** will do:
158	
159	- The clip count and the total length before and after, for example `3 clips · 00:00:12:00 → 00:00:06:00`.
160	- One line for each clip whose transition starts playing, gets longer or gets shorter:
161	  - `clip 7 gains a 0.67 s cross dissolve`
162	  - `clip 7's cross dissolve grows to 1.50 s`
163	  - `clip 7's cross dissolve shrinks to 0.67 s`
164	- When a selected clip has a speed ramp, "Each speed ramp keeps its shape: the rates it names scale with the base rate."
165	
166	A clip that couldn't take the new rate counts at its old length, and the rest of the selection still counts.
167	
168	## Apply the change
169	
170	**Apply** sets the rate on every listed clip as one undo step, **Set Speed**. Captions the change re-times are part of the same step, which is then named **Set Speed and Re-time Captions**. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
171	
172	If nothing would change, **Apply** closes the sheet and adds no undo step.
173	
174	If the rate takes a clip with sound above ×12, an alert comes first, such as "“interview.mov” will be silent at ×20."
175	
176	- **Set Speed** closes the sheet and applies the change.
177	- **Cancel** leaves the sheet up with nothing applied.
178	
179	See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
180	
181	## What a speed change does
182	
183	- **The clip's start stays and its length changes.** A faster clip can leave a gap after it, and later clips don't move up to fill it. [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) closes it.
184	- **The new length snaps to a whole frame**, and never runs past the end of the file at the new rate. See [The new length](/speed/fit-to-duration/#the-new-length).
185	- **Actions keep their places** as fractions of the clip's length.
186	- **On a ramped clip** the sheet sets the clip's own rate, its base rate, and scales the whole ramp with it. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
187	
188	A speed ramp works the other way round: it leaves the clip where it is and changes how much of the source plays.
189	
190	## A slowed clip overlapping the next
191	
192	A slower clip gets longer, so it can run into the clip after it. Later clips stay where they are, so the two now overlap.
193	
194	- **If the overlap is allowed**, the later clip gets a transition across it, and the readout names that transition.
195	- **If it isn't allowed**, the slowed clip keeps its old speed. Any other selected clips still change.
196	
197	An overlap is allowed up to half the length of the shorter clip. It isn't allowed when one of the clips is an adjustment clip, or when the clip would reach a second neighbour on the same side. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
198	
199	## Good to know
200	
201	- **Clips at different rates.** The field opens on ×1, and **Apply** sets every listed clip to the rate in the field, even if you only changed **Preserve pitch**. Choose **Cancel** to leave them at their own rates.
202	- **Preserve pitch** applies to every listed clip, and changing it alone counts as a change.
203	- **Linked clips.** Frame Job won't change the speed of a clip linked to its detached sound until you attach it. See [Linked clips](/speed/overview/#linked-clips).
204	- **Inside a nest**, the sheet works on the clips you've selected in the open nest.
205	
206	## With an agent
207	
208	`set_speed` does the same job, one clip at a time. Give it `clip` and exactly one of `rate` or `duration`, the length that [Fit to](/speed/fit-to-duration/) takes. Both or neither is an error, and so is a rate of zero or less. Leave out `keep_pitch` and the clip's setting stays as it is.
209	
210	An agent isn't asked about ×12: the reply says which clips lost their sound. Its undo step is named **Speed**. See [`set_speed`](/mcp/tools-speed/#set_speed).

235	## Fit a clip
236	
237	<Steps>
238	
239	1. Select one or more clips of a video or audio file.
240	
241	2. In the **Clip** tab's **Clip** sub-tab, open the **Speed** section.
242	
243	3. Type a length in **Fit to**, then press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>. The tooltip reads "Type a length: the rate changes so the clip plays in it".
244	
245	</Steps>
246	
247	The field takes a timecode such as `00:00:12:15` or `00:00:12.500`, a shorter form such as `01:30`, or a number of seconds such as `12.5`. Text that isn't a time beeps, and the field goes back to the clip's length.
248	
249	With several clips selected, each one is fitted to that length, as one undo step, **Fit to Duration**. Captions the change re-times are part of the same step, which is then named **Fit to Duration and Re-time Captions**.
250	
251	The field shows the first selected clip's length, with a **mixed** tag when the selected clips' lengths differ.
252	
253	Fit to lives only in the inspector. The Speed sheet has no Fit to control.
254	
255	## The new length
256	
257	The length you type snaps to the frame grid. A length that snaps to zero or less shows an error and changes nothing. Typing the clip's current length changes nothing.
258	
259	The same applies to any speed change: the clip's new length snaps to a whole frame, and never runs past the end of its file at the new rate.
260	
261	The rate is still held to ×0.1 – ×1000. A length that needs a rate past a limit stops at that limit, so the clip ends up a different length from the one you typed. For example, a 10 s clip at ×1 fitted to 200 s stops at ×0.1 and lasts 100 s.
262	
263	On a clip with a speed ramp, Fit to scales the whole ramp. It stops where any rate in the ramp would pass a limit, and the clip ends up a different length in the same way. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
264	
265	Everything else works as it does for any speed change:
266	
267	- The clip's start stays where it is, and later clips don't move.
268	- A fit that runs into the next clip follows the [overlap rule](/speed/change-speed/#a-slowed-clip-overlapping-the-next).
269	- A fit that takes a clip with sound past ×12 asks first, with **Set Speed** and **Cancel**. **Cancel** puts the field back. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
270	
271	## When Fit to is unavailable
272	
273	- **An action is selected.** Fit to belongs to the clip and can't be set inside an action, so its row is marked ⊘. Anything you type there changes the whole clip, not the action.
274	- **The selection holds another kind of clip.** The Speed section appears only when every selected clip is a media clip.
275	- **The clip is linked to its detached sound.** Frame Job won't change its speed until you attach it. See [Linked clips](/speed/overview/#linked-clips).
276	
277	## With an agent
278	
279	`set_speed` with `duration` in place of `rate` does the same job, one clip at a time. A duration of zero or less is an error. See [`set_speed`](/mcp/tools-speed/#set_speed).

334	## Reset the rate
335	
336	**Reset** in the section header sets the rate back to ×1, as one undo step, **Set Speed**. It leaves **Keep pitch** as it is.

340	## Rate inside an action
341	
342	While an action is selected, **Rate** shows and sets the rate that action ends on. Setting it turns any action into a Speed action, which is how you [build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).

359	## Clear a rate from an action
360

371	## Rows that stay the clip's
372	
373	**Keep pitch** and **Fit to** change the clip itself even with an action selected, so they're marked ⊘ and never animate.

396	
397	A rate stretch changes a clip's length by changing its speed, not by trimming it. The clip still plays all of the source it showed, faster or slower, so it's the quick way to make a shot fit by eye.

400	  keys="⌥-drag"

404	
405	## Stretch a clip
406	
407	<Steps>
408	
409	1. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd>.
410	
411	2. Press on the **end** edge of a clip of a video or audio file, and drag. The timeline shows the result as you drag.
412	
413	3. Let go.
414	
415	</Steps>
416	
417	The stretch lands as one undo step, **Rate Stretch**. The new rate is the length of source the clip shows divided by its new length, so a 10 s clip at ×1 dragged to 5 s plays at ×2.
418	
419	Frame Job reads <kbd>⌥</kbd> when you press, so hold it before the drag starts. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on an edge is a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), not a stretch.
420	
421	Actions keep their fraction of the clip. Captions over the clip are re-timed in the same step, which is then named **Rate Stretch and Re-time Captions**, and they jump when you let go. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
422	
423	## Snapping
424	
425	A rate stretch snaps like any other edge drag. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> as you press to turn snapping off for that drag. See [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/).
426	
427	## Which edges and clips stretch
428	
429	| You drag with ⌥ | What happens |
430	| --- | --- |
431	| A media clip's end edge | A rate stretch |
432	| A clip's start edge | An ordinary trim |
433	| The end edge of a still, text, shape, graphic or any other clip | An ordinary trim, with the undo step **Trim Clip** |
434	| An edge on a locked track | Nothing. The edge doesn't move. |
435	| The end edge of a clip linked to its detached sound | Nothing, until you [attach it](/audio/detach-and-attach/) |
436	
437	## Where a stretch stops
438	
439	The clip stops following the drag when the next step would break a limit, and it lands at the last length that worked:
440	
441	- **Rate limits.** The stretch can't need a rate outside ×0.1 – ×1000.
442	- **One frame.** The clip can't get shorter than one frame.
443	- **The next clip.** A stretch into the next clip follows the same [overlap rule](/speed/change-speed/#a-slowed-clip-overlapping-the-next) as any slowed clip, so the later clip gains a transition across an allowed overlap.
444	
445	Drag back inside the limit and the clip follows you again.
446	
447	## A ramped clip
448	
449	On a clip with a speed ramp, the whole ramp stretches with the clip and keeps its shape. The stretch stops where any of its rates would pass the limits. See [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/).
450	
451	## Stretching past ×12
452	
453	If a stretch takes a clip with sound past ×12, Frame Job puts the stretch back and asks first.
454	
455	- **Set Speed** applies the stretch you made.
456	- **Cancel** leaves the clip as it was.
457	
458	See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
459	
460	## With an agent
461	
462	`rate_stretch` takes `clip` and `to_end`, the clip's new end on the timeline, and both are required. A text, shape, image or freeze clip is an error. The reply's `captions_retimed` lists the captions that moved, and `captions_removed` those whose speech the clip no longer plays. See [`rate_stretch`](/mcp/tools-speed/#rate_stretch).
